title: Skills
summary: A skill is a portable folder of instructions, references and scripts (the agentskills.io format) that an agent loads on demand. Only a short description sits in the prompt until the skill is needed.
useIf: You have reusable domain procedures (expense policy, report templates, data checks) that would bloat the system prompt if always loaded.
avoidIf: The behaviour is one short rule that belongs in the instructions, or the API is too unstable for your release gate: the skills API is experimental.

explain.md: A skill is a directory with a required `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter plus markdown) and optional `scripts/`, `references/` and `assets/`. Required frontmatter: `name` (max 64 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, matching the directory name) and `description` (max 1,024 characters, saying what it does and when to use it) [[tr7]]. Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines and move detail into reference files.

**Progressive disclosure** keeps context small: (1) **advertise** about 100 tokens per skill in the system prompt each run, (2) **load** the full body with `load_skill` (under 5,000 tokens recommended), (3) **read resources** with `read_skill_resource`, (4) **run scripts** with `run_skill_script`. `load_skill` is always advertised; the other two only when some skill has resources or scripts [[tr7]].

explain.title: How a skill reaches the model

steps.title: Advertise
steps.md: Name and description, about 100 tokens each.

steps.title: Run
steps.md: `run_skill_script` needs a script runner you supply.

explain.md: **Sources.** File-based (folders with SKILL.md), code-defined (`AgentInlineSkill` / `InlineSkill`), class-based, and MCP-based (`UseMcpSkills` / `MCPSkillsSource`). The provider (`AgentSkillsProvider` in C#, `SkillsProvider` in Python) is a context provider. **Approval:** in the Harness all three skill tools require approval by default, and without a script runner script execution fails. Auto-approve only trusted read-only tools, for example `AgentSkillsProvider.ReadOnlyToolsAutoApprovalRule` [[tr7]]. The Harness enables skills by default in .NET (discovering from the current directory) and opt-in in Python through `skills_paths` or `skills_provider`.

explain.title: expense-report/SKILL.md
explain.code:
---
name: expense-report
description: File and validate employee expense reports according to company policy. Use when asked about expense submissions, reimbursement rules, or spending limits.
license: Apache-2.0
metadata:
  version: "2.1"
---
# Steps
1. Load references/POLICY_FAQ.md for limits.
2. Run scripts/validate.py on the draft.

blocks.code:
skills = SkillsProvider.from_paths(skill_paths=Path(__file__).parent / 'skills')
agent = Agent(client=client, instructions='You are helpful.',
              context_providers=[skills])

# or on the Harness:
agent = create_harness_agent(client, skills_paths=['./skills'])

explain.title: Experimental API (checked 2026-10-13)
explain.md: The skills API had breaking changes in python 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 (May 2026), including folder discovery moving to the agentskills.io layout. The 1.0 GA blog listed Skills as preview [[tr7]] [[tr41]].

whereToUse: Company procedures: expense rules, security review checklists, support playbooks
Agents shared by many teams, where each team adds a skill folder instead of editing prompts
Skills reused across Agent Skills-compatible products because the format is an open spec
Long procedures with scripts, such as validators or generators, that the model should run rather than imitate

use: You have many procedures and only a few apply to any one request
Content changes by domain owners, not developers, and should ship as files
You want auditable, versioned behaviour packages
avoid: One or two short rules: put them in the instructions
You cannot supply a safe script runner but the skill depends on scripts
Sources are untrusted: skill text and scripts steer the agent and may execute code
flips: Skill sources come from an MCP server you do not control: keep approval on for all three skill tools
The skill count grows past the point where advertising costs matter (100 tokens each): filter or aggregate sources with the skill source decorators

pitfalls.cause: Invalid YAML, a duplicate recognised field, wrong field casing, or `name` not matching the directory prevents loading
pitfalls.fix: Use the lowercase field names from the spec, keep `name` equal to the folder, validate with a loader test

pitfalls.symptom: Script execution fails in the Harness
pitfalls.cause: No script runner was supplied for file-based scripts
pitfalls.fix: Pass an `AgentFileSkillScriptRunner` (C#) or a runner in Python, and keep `run_skill_script` behind approval

pitfalls.cause: The experimental API changed in python 1.3.0 and 1.4.0
pitfalls.fix: Pin versions and read the significant-changes page before upgrading

scenarios.title: Forty procedures, one assistant
scenarios.situation: A finance assistant must follow forty procedures owned by different teams. Each request touches one or two. Prompt size already costs money and latency.
unknowns: Are the folders from trusted owners only?
scenarios.question: How do you package them?

options.name: One skill per procedure, file-based, with read-only auto-approval and script approval kept on
options.why: About 4,000 tokens to advertise 40 skills (40 x 100) instead of loading all bodies, owners edit files, scripts stay gated.
options.tradeoff: Extra tool calls to load, an experimental API, and advertising cost still grows with count.

options.name: One big system prompt containing every procedure
options.why: Pays all tokens on every request and degrades attention.
options.tradeoff: Fine for under five short rules.

options.name: A retrieval context provider over the procedure documents
options.tradeoff: No scripts or step structure; retrieval may miss a needed step.

flips.then: Use retrieval to find candidates and skills for the few that matter, or filter sources per user.

flips.if: Procedures must be identical for every run and audited

scenarios.takeaway: Skills trade extra load calls for a small standing prompt.

scenarios.title: Third-party skills from a registry
scenarios.situation: A platform team wants agents to pull skills from an external MCP server so partners can publish procedures. Some skills include scripts.
unknowns: Is there a sandbox for scripts?
scenarios.question: What is your stance?

options.name: Allow reading skills, keep approval on for all three skill tools, run scripts only in a sandbox runner, vet publishers
options.why: Skill text steers the model and scripts execute code, so both need gating.
options.tradeoff: Friction for users and engineering work for the sandbox.

options.name: Auto-approve all skill tools for speed
options.why: An untrusted skill could steer the agent into privileged tools or run code.
options.tradeoff: Only acceptable for skill sources you wrote and review.

options.name: Block external skills entirely
options.tradeoff: Loses the partner ecosystem you wanted.

flips.if: The publisher set is closed and signed
flips.then: Relax to read-only auto-approval for those sources.

flips.if: Scripts are removed from the package format you accept
flips.then: Approval for `run_skill_script` becomes moot, but keep reviewing instruction text.

scenarios.takeaway: A skill is code and prompt at once: trust it like a dependency.

quiz.q: An agent has 30 skills. Each advertisement costs about 100 tokens. How many tokens does advertising add to the system prompt on every run?
quiz.explain: 30 skills x about 100 tokens = about 3,000 tokens, before any skill body is loaded. Bodies load only through `load_skill` and should stay under 5,000 tokens each.

quiz.q: In the Harness, what is the default approval behaviour of the skill tools?
options: Approval applies only to MCP-based skills
quiz.explain: All three require approval by default; use a read-only auto-approval rule only for sources you trust.

flashcards.front: Name the four stages of skill progressive disclosure.
flashcards.back: Advertise (about 100 tokens each), load (`load_skill`, under 5,000 tokens), read resources, run scripts.
`name` max 64 chars, lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, equal to the folder name. `description` max 1,024 chars.

flashcards.front: Which SDK enables skills by default in the Harness?
flashcards.back: .NET enables them by default; Python makes them opt-in via `skills_paths` or `skills_provider`.
